Architecture Diagram

The ServiceFabric scope deploys two web application containers and a SQL Server container as separate Service Fabric application types. Application source code is not included in this subdirectory, so the diagrams describe deployment boundaries and manifest-declared communication only.

Data Storage & External Services

The two web service manifests configure their SQL connection to the separately deployed eshopmodernized.sqldata service at port 1433. Azure Storage, Azure Active Directory, and Application Insights are represented by configurable environment settings; the checked-in service defaults disable these options or leave their values empty. The application containers’ internal implementation is outside this directory.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • Each web application and the SQL container are independently packaged as a Service Fabric application type with a singleton partition.
  • The front ends connect to SQL using a Service Fabric DNS name rather than a container IP address.
  • Service Fabric manifests bind container port 80 to front-end ports 5115 and 5114, and port 1433 to SQL.

No CPU or memory limits are declared in the application manifests reviewed.

Startup Dependency Chain

  1. Provision the Service Fabric cluster and its network/storage/certificate resources through ARM deployment.
  2. Deploy the SQL application so eshopmodernized.sqldata:1433 is available.
  3. Deploy the MVC and Web Forms applications, which reference that SQL DNS name.

The application manifests do not declare a SQL startup dependency, health-check wait, or retry chain. The deployment scripts and cluster-level readiness behavior are outside the application manifests.

Secrets Provisioning Workflow

Cluster administrator credentials and certificate references are inputs to ARM deployment; the templates expose source-vault and certificate URL parameters. Cloud application parameters substitute external storage, telemetry, and Azure AD values into environment variables. No managed identity permissions or automated secret retrieval workflow are specified in this directory. The checked-in SQL service manifest contains a static database password, so secret provisioning is not fully externalized for that container.

Dependency Map

The ServiceFabric deployment solution declares one unique NuGet build dependency, shared by three application projects. Container images are declared in service manifests and are deployment artifacts, not package references.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The deployment projects target .NET Framework 4.6.1 or 4.6.2 and use the legacy Service Fabric MSBuild package 1.6.1. These are older deployment technologies; validate compatibility with the installed Service Fabric tooling and supported Windows container images before changing the build environment.

Notable Observations

  • The repository scope contains deployment projects and manifests, not application .csproj files or application source dependency manifests.
  • The three projects repeat the same Service Fabric MSBuild package declaration; no central package management is present.
  • The service manifests reference SQL Server 2017 and untagged web container images; these are image dependencies rather than NuGet dependencies.
